title: 东北硬菜④完结·小鸡炖蘑菇：姑爷进门，为啥小鸡要“断魂” | Northeast Comfort Food P4 · Chicken & Mushroom 🍲
description:
锅包肉、铁锅炖、猪肉炖粉条、小鸡炖蘑菇——你心里的东北硬菜天花板，是哪一道？ / Of all four, which is your ultimate Dongbei dish?

第④集·完结·小鸡炖蘑菇 —— 「东北硬菜」系列收官，每天一道东北招牌菜。
P4 · Finale · Chicken & Mushroom Stew — the closing chapter of Northeast Comfort Food.

东北有句老话：「姑爷进门，小鸡断魂。」新姑爷第一次陪媳妇回门，老丈人家必做的一道菜，就是小鸡炖蘑菇——这是招待贵客的最高规格。要选一只养了半年以上、满地跑的笨鸡，配上东北山里的野生榛蘑，小火咕嘟一个多小时；榛蘑吸饱了鸡汤，往往比鸡肉还香。它是年三十桌上的压轴主菜，也是「东北四大炖」之一。据《奉天通志》，清末闯关东时期，伐木工人把猎到的野鸡和秋天采晒的榛蘑同煮，就是它最初的雏形。锅包肉、铁锅炖、猪肉炖粉条，一路走到这，压轴的正是这一锅。
There's an old Dongbei saying: “when the son-in-law arrives, the chicken meets its doom.” The first time a new son-in-law comes home with his wife, the one dish the family must make is chicken stewed with mushrooms — the highest honor for a guest. You pick a free-range hen raised over half a year, pair it with wild hazel mushrooms from the northeastern hills, and simmer low for more than an hour; the mushrooms soak up the broth until they out-taste the meat itself. It's the centerpiece of New Year's Eve and one of the “four great Dongbei stews.” Per the Fengtian Gazetteer, its earliest form was loggers during the Manchurian migration cooking wild fowl with autumn-dried hazel mushrooms. Guobaorou, iron-pot stew, pork-and-glass-noodles — and this pot crowns them all.
